key_insight: Careful 3D-specific training design — adding 3D data augmentation and avoiding/adapting Batch Normalization — unlocks stable, scalable 3D policy learning, enabled by a transformer-based 3D encoder paired with a diffusion decoder.
problem_solved: Addresses training instabilities and severe overfitting that prevented adoption of powerful 3D perception models for 3D policy learning and cross-embodiment transfer.
method: Systematic diagnosis: identify missing 3D data augmentation and harmful effects of Batch Normalization as primary failure modes.
Architecture: couple a scalable transformer-based 3D encoder with a diffusion-based decoder to improve representation robustness and downstream policy generation.
Training recipe: introduce explicit 3D augmentations and replace/adjust BN (e.g., alternatives or ablations) plus stability-focused training practices to reduce overfitting.
impact: Makes it practical to train robust, generalizable 3D policies that leverage modern 3D perception backbones, improving cross-embodiment transfer and accelerating deployment in robotics, simulation, and embodied AI research.
visual_elements: Failure diagnosis flowchart: show path from missing 3D augmentations / BN issues → instability / overfitting → blocked model adoption
Model diagram: transformer-based 3D encoder feeding a diffusion decoder with callouts for where augmentations and BN changes are applied
Training plots: learning curves and generalization metrics comparing baseline vs. proposed recipe (stability and overfitting reduction)
Qualitative panel: cross-embodiment task examples showing improved policy transfer (different robot bodies/environments)
paper_authors: Zhengdong Hong, Shenrui Wu, Haozhe Cui, Boyi Zhao, Ran Ji
